# nonconform

> Conformal p-values, FDR-controlled anomaly discovery, and exchangeability-martingale change monitoring in Python.

This file is a concise, AI-readable map of the public documentation for nonconform.

## Documentation

- [Home](https://oliverhennhoefer.github.io/nonconform/) - Project overview, citation, guarantee scope, and installation links.
- [Installation](https://oliverhennhoefer.github.io/nonconform/installation/) - Package installation and optional extras.
- [Quick Start](https://oliverhennhoefer.github.io/nonconform/quickstart/) - Minimal batch-discovery and sequential-monitoring workflows.
- [User Guide](https://oliverhennhoefer.github.io/nonconform/user_guide/) - Concepts, strategies, weighting, FDR control, martingales, evaluation, and troubleshooting.
- [API Reference](https://oliverhennhoefer.github.io/nonconform/api/) - Public API modules and compatibility contract.
- [Common Workflows](https://oliverhennhoefer.github.io/nonconform/api/common_workflows/) - Independent copy-paste examples for the main public calls.
- [Examples](https://oliverhennhoefer.github.io/nonconform/examples/) - Classical, conditional, resampling, weighted, derandomized e-value, and FDR examples.

## Key Topic Pages

- [Understanding Conformal Inference](https://oliverhennhoefer.github.io/nonconform/user_guide/conformal_inference/) - Conformal p-values, calibration assumptions, and interpretation.
- [Choosing Calibration Strategies](https://oliverhennhoefer.github.io/nonconform/user_guide/choosing_strategies/) - Split, cross-validation, jackknife, and bootstrap trade-offs.
- [Weighted Conformal P-values](https://oliverhennhoefer.github.io/nonconform/user_guide/weighted_conformal/) - Covariate shift, importance weighting, diagnostics, and WCS selection.
- [False Discovery Rate Control](https://oliverhennhoefer.github.io/nonconform/user_guide/fdr_control/) - raw-score FPR certificates, FDR-controlled anomaly decisions, and online FDR workflows.
- [Derandomized E-Values](https://oliverhennhoefer.github.io/nonconform/user_guide/fdr_control/#derandomized-conformal-e-values) - Uniformly aggregated repeated split-conformal evidence with e-BH.
- [Exchangeability Martingales](https://oliverhennhoefer.github.io/nonconform/user_guide/exchangeability_martingales/) - Sequential conformal ranks, evidence processes, and alarm semantics.
- [Streaming Evaluation](https://oliverhennhoefer.github.io/nonconform/user_guide/streaming_evaluation/) - Separate evaluation designs for point anomalies and persistent changes.
- [API Stability](https://oliverhennhoefer.github.io/nonconform/api/stability/) - v1 public API and statistical validity compatibility policy.

## Notes for AI Assistants

- Treat documented statistical guarantees as conditional on the assumptions stated in the relevant guide pages.
- For one fixed batch family, prefer `ConformalDetector.select(...)`; it applies BH for p-value strategies, e-BH with `DerandomizedSplits`, and WCS in weighted mode. E-value diagnostics are in `last_selection_result`; strategy ties are randomized automatically from a separate fitting-derived seed.
- For simultaneous realized-FDP certification, use detector.fdp_bounds(x, confidence=...) or a native result.fdp_bounds(confidence=...); these confidence-only calls prepare one default MC-THC envelope with 1000 fresh draws, boost=True, lower=.01, upper=.99, beta=.5. Certificates own immutable fixed-family evidence; threshold queries never resample. select(t) means p<=t, not a target FDP. Coverage is joint over the data and fresh independent Monte Carlo sampling, not conditional on every fixed seed or realized envelope. Keep the scoring map and family fixed; do not cherry-pick repeated constructions. Only unweighted empirical Split/detached native scopes are supported. FDPCertificate.from_p_values is the expert route for confidence, method, n_resamples, seed, boost, lower, upper, and beta in (0,1]; method-specific unused options must be omitted. Precision is an internal solver detail. Choose all settings before inspecting bounds. A fixed seed reproduces an expert envelope but does not provide a separate conditional coverage guarantee. Expert method="ks" uses the dependent-law transductive DKW construction, not the ordinary i.i.d. one-sample KS distribution.
- For raw-score threshold certification, use detector.fpr_bounds(confidence=...) or a native result.fpr_bounds(confidence=...); FPRCertificate.from_scores is the expert route. It uses anomalous-higher calibration scores and the exact finite-sample one-sided KS distribution, evaluated deterministically with no simulation parameters. Use threshold_for(target_fpr) and select(scores, target_fpr=...). Native scope is unweighted Split/detached calibration independently of the p-value estimator. Coverage requires clean calibration and future inlier scores that are i.i.d. from the same distribution conditional on a score map fixed independently of calibration; exchangeability alone is insufficient. With probability at least confidence over the calibration draw, the certificate bounds the population inlier FPR simultaneously at every threshold, conditional on the realized calibration sample and independently fitted score map. On that event, the chosen threshold's future-inlier false-alarm probability is at most target_fpr. This differs from marginal conformal validity averaged over calibration draws and from ConditionalEmpirical's p-value transformation. The finite-threshold floor is about 3.85% at n_calibration=1000 and confidence=.95; lower targets yield infinity and an empty selection. threshold_for returns a NumPy float64 scalar; preserve its dtype for direct score comparisons. This does not guarantee FDR/FDP, recall, realized finite-batch proportions, batch-wide no-false-alarm probability, or sequential Ville control.
- For one ordered change-monitoring stream, use `ExchangeabilityMonitor`; fixed-calibration batch p-values are not sequential conformal p-values.
- Keep expected FDR, realized FDP, and one-stream Ville false-alarm control distinct.
- Keep `nonconform._internal` private; it is not user-facing API.
